## Notes

Guide: [claude-code.md](../claude-code.md)

### `create`

**Create note**

Save a new note. The body is plain text; put #hashtags in it to tag the note (tags are parsed from the body). Returns the created note with its new id (like A-B32) - quote that id to the user. Pass origin when saving from inside a repository.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | yes | The full note text, including any #hashtags. Must not be empty. |
| `origin` | object |  | Where this note is being saved from. Pass it whenever you save from inside a repository. |
| `origin.cwd` | string |  | Absolute working directory of the Claude Code session. |
| `origin.repo` | string |  | Repository name or remote, e.g. "seer" or "github.com/me/seer". |
| `origin.claude_session` | string |  | Claude Code session id, if known. |

### `get`

**Get notes** · read-only

Fetch one or several notes by id. Returns { notes, missing, deleted }: missing lists inputs that are not ids or match no note; deleted lists ids of soft-deleted notes (pass include_deleted=true to see their bodies, or restore them).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | string[] | yes | One or more note ids, e.g. ["A-B32"] or ["ab32", "7-QX0"]. |
| `include_deleted` | boolean |  | Also return soft-deleted notes (they carry deleted_at). Default false. |

### `update`

**Replace note body**

Replace the whole body of a note with new text. Read the note with get first and send the complete new text: anything you leave out is removed. Tags are re-parsed from the new body, so keep the #hashtags you want (add one to tag the note). The previous body is kept as a revision. Fails on a deleted note.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |
| `body` | string | yes | The complete new note text. Must not be empty; use delete to remove a note. |
| `origin` | object |  | Where this note is being saved from. Pass it whenever you save from inside a repository. |
| `origin.cwd` | string |  | Absolute working directory of the Claude Code session. |
| `origin.repo` | string |  | Repository name or remote, e.g. "seer" or "github.com/me/seer". |
| `origin.claude_session` | string |  | Claude Code session id, if known. |

### `append`

**Append to note**

Add text to the end of a note, after a blank line, leaving the existing text untouched. Hashtags in the appended text become tags. The previous body is kept as a revision. Fails on a deleted note.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |
| `text` | string | yes | Text to add at the end. |

### `delete`

**Delete note**

Soft-delete a note: it disappears from list, search and tags, but its text is kept and restore brings it back. Deleting an already deleted note changes nothing.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |

### `restore`

**Restore note**

Undo a delete. Use list with deleted="only" to find deleted notes. Restoring a note that is not deleted changes nothing.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |

### `list`

**List notes** · read-only

List notes newest first, optionally filtered by tags and a date range. Use it for "my notes on #seer this week", "my last note about #v250" (tags_any=["v250"], limit=1) or one side of a comparison (call it once per side, then compare yourself). Returns { notes, next_cursor }; when next_cursor is not null there are more notes - pass it back as cursor to get the next page. Filter notes with images by has_image (true = at least one image), and by when a photo was taken with taken_from/taken_to (EXIF; a note matches when any of its images does). To look at the pictures, pass the note ids to view_images.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tags_any` | string[] |  | Notes that carry at least one of these tags. "seer" and "#seer" are the same. |
| `tags_all` | string[] |  | Notes that carry every one of these tags. |
| `date_field` | "created" \| "updated" |  | Which date from/to filter on, and (for list) the sort order. Default "created". |
| `from` | string |  | Inclusive start: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `to` | string |  | Inclusive end: YYYY-MM-DD (the whole local day is included) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `has_image` | boolean |  | true: only notes with at least one image (photos, screenshots). false: only notes with no image. Omit for both. |
| `taken_from` | string |  | Earliest EXIF "taken" date: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. A note matches when any of its images was taken in range; images without a camera date never match. For the day a picture was SAVED use from/to instead. |
| `taken_to` | string |  | Latest EXIF "taken" date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (the whole local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. Same any-image rule as taken_from. |
| `deleted` | "exclude" \| "include" \| "only" |  | Soft-deleted notes: "exclude" (default), "include", or "only" (to find something to restore). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size, 1-200. Default 50. |
| `cursor` | string |  | next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged. Omit for the first page. |

### `search`

**Search notes** · read-only

Search notes by meaning as well as by words, with the same tag and date filters as list. By default (mode "hybrid") it understands what the query means, not only its words: "ArangoDB credentials" finds a note saying "arango root password is in the vault", so pass the question in plain words. Results blend word matches, closeness in meaning, matching tags and recency; a note id, code identifier or version string that appears word for word still ranks first. mode "text" is exact-word full-text search only: no stemming; supports "quoted phrases", OR, and -word to exclude; ranked by relevance, then recency. Returns { notes, next_cursor, mode, fallback? }: mode is the ranking actually used; fallback is present when meaning search was unavailable and the results are word matches only - tell the user. Filter notes with images by has_image (true = at least one image), and by when a photo was taken with taken_from/taken_to (EXIF; a note matches when any of its images does). To look at the pictures, pass the note ids to view_images.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | What to look for: a plain question ("have we seen auth failures after resume?") or exact terms ("retry backoff", "\"connection pool\" -redis"). |
| `mode` | "hybrid" \| "text" |  | "hybrid" (default): meaning + words + tags + recency. "text": exact-word full-text search only. |
| `tags_any` | string[] |  | Notes that carry at least one of these tags. "seer" and "#seer" are the same. |
| `tags_all` | string[] |  | Notes that carry every one of these tags. |
| `date_field` | "created" \| "updated" |  | Which date from/to filter on, and (for list) the sort order. Default "created". |
| `from` | string |  | Inclusive start: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `to` | string |  | Inclusive end: YYYY-MM-DD (the whole local day is included) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `has_image` | boolean |  | true: only notes with at least one image (photos, screenshots). false: only notes with no image. Omit for both. |
| `taken_from` | string |  | Earliest EXIF "taken" date: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. A note matches when any of its images was taken in range; images without a camera date never match. For the day a picture was SAVED use from/to instead. |
| `taken_to` | string |  | Latest EXIF "taken" date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (the whole local day) or an ISO 8601 datetime. Same any-image rule as taken_from. |
| `deleted` | "exclude" \| "include" \| "only" |  | Soft-deleted notes: "exclude" (default), "include", or "only" (to find something to restore). |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size, 1-200. Default 50. |
| `cursor` | string |  | next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged. Omit for the first page. |

### `tags`

**List tags** · read-only

Every tag used by a live note, most used first, with its note count and last_used (the newest updated_at among its notes). Use it to discover what the user tags things with before filtering.

No arguments.

### `related`

**Related notes** · read-only

Notes closest in meaning to one note, most similar first, each with a similarity score (1 = same meaning, near 0 = unrelated). Finds notes that share no words with it. Never includes the note itself or deleted notes. Use it for "what else do I have on this?" or "notes related to A-B32" after finding a note with get, list or search. Returns { note_id, related: [{ note, similarity }] }. Fails on a deleted note and on a photo that has no text.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many related notes to return, 1-50. Default 10. |

### `revisions`

**List revisions** · read-only

Earlier bodies of a note, newest first. Each has a revision number, the body as it was, and saved_at (when it was replaced). Pass a revision number to revert to restore that text.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |

### `revert`

**Revert to revision**

Make a note's body equal to one of its earlier revisions (numbers come from revisions). The body being replaced is kept as a new revision, so a revert can itself be undone.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted ("ab32" works). |
| `revision` | integer | yes | Revision number from revisions(id). |

## Photos

Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md)

### `create_image`

**Create image note**

Save an image as a new note with that one image. Give exactly one of path or image_id (in Claude Code, pasted_image N stands in for image_id when the prompt context gave the picture no id). path: a local image file (screenshot, photo, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/HEIC/TIFF...), absolute or starting with ~/; the file is COPIED byte for byte into the notes store and the source is left where it is. image_id: a picture the user PASTED into a chat, by its CHAT image id like G-0NC (the wall chat shows it as [image upload:ID]; a Claude Code /n prompt lists the pasted images by id). This is a chat image id, NOT a note image id from a note's images[].id. Use image_id, never a path, for a pasted picture. Optional body is the note text; #hashtags in it become tags. If the exact same picture already lives in a note, that note is returned (created: false) instead of a duplicate. Non-image files are refused. Returns { note, created }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Absolute path to a local image file, or a path starting with ~/. Omit when giving image_id. |
| `image_id` | string |  | Chat image id of a pasted picture, like G-0NC (shown as [image upload:ID]). Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note image id. Omit when giving path. |
| `pasted_image` | integer |  | Claude Code only: the N of "[Image #N]" for a picture pasted into this very prompt when the /n context gave it no id. The notes-paste hook uploads it and swaps in image_id before the call runs. Give it instead of path and image_id, never with them. |
| `body` | string |  | Text for the note. #hashtags become tags. |
| `origin` | object |  | Where this note came from. Pass the current cwd/repo when saving from a repo. |
| `origin.cwd` | string |  | Working directory the note was saved from. |
| `origin.repo` | string |  | Repository name or remote. |
| `origin.claude_session` | string |  | Claude Code session id. |

### `view_images`

**View images**

Look at the pictures in notes. Takes 1 to 8 ids (any case, dash optional): a note id shows every image of that note in order, an image id (from a note's images[].id) shows that one image. An image id equals its note id for a note's first image, so a bare id means the NOTE; write img:ID (for example img:9-TD6) to mean that one picture wherever it lives now. Each picture comes after its metadata (note id, image id and "image k of n", saved date, EXIF taken date, dimensions, tags, body), downscaled to at most 1568 px on the long edge. Find ids first with list/search (has_image: true means at least one image). At most 8 images come back per call; a last text line lists the image ids left out, to pass to the next call. Text notes, deleted notes, removed images, unknown ids and images whose file lives on another machine come back as a text line saying so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | string[] | yes | Note ids or image ids, 1 to 8. |

### `attach_image`

**Attach image to note**

Add an image to an existing note; a note can hold several images, kept in attach order. Give the note id and exactly one of path or image_id (in Claude Code, pasted_image N stands in for image_id when the prompt context gave the picture no id). path: a local image file (screenshot, photo, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/HEIC/TIFF...), absolute or starting with ~/; the file is COPIED byte for byte into the notes store and the source is left where it is. image_id: a picture the user PASTED into a chat, by its CHAT image id like G-0NC (the wall chat shows it as [image upload:ID]; a Claude Code /n prompt lists the pasted images by id). This is a chat image id, NOT a note image id from a note's images[].id. Use image_id, never a path, for a pasted picture. If the exact same picture already lives in a note (this one or another), nothing is copied and that note is returned with attached: false: tell the user which note holds it (a deleted holder note is restored). The note must not be deleted (restore it first). Non-image files are refused. Returns { note, attached }; a new image is the last entry of note.images.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32 to attach to. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |
| `path` | string |  | Absolute path to a local image file, or a path starting with ~/. Omit when giving image_id. |
| `image_id` | string |  | Chat image id of a pasted picture, like G-0NC (shown as [image upload:ID]). Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note image id. Omit when giving path. |
| `pasted_image` | integer |  | Claude Code only: the N of "[Image #N]" for a picture pasted into this very prompt when the /n context gave it no id. The notes-paste hook uploads it and swaps in image_id before the call runs. Give it instead of path and image_id, never with them. |
| `origin` | object |  | Where this note came from. Pass the current cwd/repo when saving from a repo. |
| `origin.cwd` | string |  | Working directory the note was saved from. |
| `origin.repo` | string |  | Repository name or remote. |
| `origin.claude_session` | string |  | Claude Code session id. |

### `remove_image`

**Remove image from note**

Take one image out of its note. This is soft and reversible: the image moves to the recycle bin, its file stays on disk, and restore_image(image_id) puts it back at the same position. Pass the image's id (each entry of a note's images has one; the first image of a note saved from a picture has the note's own id). Removing an image that is already removed changes nothing. Returns { note }: the owning note without that image.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_id` | string | yes | Image id like A-B32 (from note.images[].id). Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |

### `restore_image`

**Restore removed image**

Undo remove_image: put a removed image back into its note at its old position. If the note itself was deleted it is restored too. Refused (duplicate_image) when the same picture has since been saved again and is live in another note; the error names that note. Returns { note }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_id` | string | yes | Id of the removed image, like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |

### `move_image`

**Move image to another note**

Move one image out of the note that holds it, without copying anything: the image keeps its id and its file, only its note changes. Without to_note_id a NEW note is created that holds only this image, with body as its text (#hashtags become tags); with to_note_id the image goes to the end of that existing note. Use it to split a picture out of a note with many pictures: look at the picture, write the text the new note should carry, then call move_image. The old note stays, one image fewer. Refused for a removed image, a deleted note, or when the image is already in to_note_id. Returns { note, from, created }: note is the note that now holds the image, from is the note it left.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_id` | string | yes | Image id like A-B32 (from note.images[].id or [note image:ID]). Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |
| `to_note_id` | string |  | Existing live note to move the image into. Omit to create a new note for it. |
| `body` | string |  | Text of the new note (only when to_note_id is omitted). #hashtags become tags. |
| `origin` | object |  | Where this note came from. Pass the current cwd/repo when saving from a repo. |
| `origin.cwd` | string |  | Working directory the note was saved from. |
| `origin.repo` | string |  | Repository name or remote. |
| `origin.claude_session` | string |  | Claude Code session id. |

### `similar_images`

**Similar images** · read-only

Find the photos that look most like a picture, or that match a description of what is in it. Give exactly one of: image_id (a picture already in the notes, from a note's images[].id), upload_id (an image pasted into the wall chat; the message names it [image upload:ID]), query (words describing the picture, e.g. "red top in a car"; words and pictures share one vector space), or pasted_image (Claude Code: the number of an image pasted into this conversation, 1 for the first). Returns { source, model, hits: [{ image_id, note_id, similarity, note: { body, tags }, available }] }, most similar first (similarity 1 = the same picture, near 0 = unrelated). Never returns the source image, a removed image or an image of a deleted note. It only measures likeness: call view_images with the top image ids and look before saying which ones match.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_id` | string |  | A picture already in the notes: an id from a note's images[].id, like A-B32. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |
| `upload_id` | string |  | An image pasted into the wall chat: the ID from "[image upload:ID]" in the message. |
| `query` | string |  | Words describing what is IN the picture, e.g. "red top in a car". For words in the note text use search instead. |
| `pasted_image` | integer |  | Claude Code only: N of "[Image #N]" for an image pasted into the conversation, 1 for the first. A pasted image has no file path; the notes-paste hook uploads it and replaces this with upload_id before the call arrives. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many images to return, 1-50. Default 10. |

## Claude Code sessions

Guide: [sessions.md](../sessions.md)

### `sessions_search`

**Search Claude Code sessions** · read-only

Find the user's past Claude Code sessions (both laptops) by meaning and words in their summaries, names, titles, prompts and commit messages, in the notes saved from or linked to each session, and in what Claude replied to each prompt, e.g. "when did I fix photo delete in the wall?". Optional repo narrows to one repository (e.g. "mcp-notes"). Returns { query, mode, fallback, hits: [{ node_id, repo, title, started_at, last_active_at, host, available, live, status, parent_node_id, fork_of, summary, via_notes, via_replies, score, url }] }, best first. fork_of is set when the session is a fork Claude Code copied from another session: "fork of <parent node id> (after prompt N, <local time>)", i.e. the parent and how many of its prompts the fork copied; null otherwise. via_notes lists the session's notes that matched ({ id, excerpt }, note ids like A-B32). via_replies lists Claude's replies in that session that matched ({ seq, excerpt }: seq is the number of the prompt the reply answered, excerpt the passage around the match). Both are best first, at most 3, and empty when the session matched on its own text. A match through a note or a reply counts a little less than the same match in the session's own summary or prompts. fallback set means meaning search was unavailable and only word matches came back. Then call session_get(node_id) for the full record.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | What the session was about, in plain words. |
| `repo` | string |  | Only sessions of this repository, e.g. "mcp-notes". Omit for every repository. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many sessions, 1-50. Default 10. |

### `session_get`

**Get a Claude Code session** · read-only

One Claude Code session by node id (like A0-3G): { session: { node_id, session_id, repo, title, name, branch, cwd, started_at, last_active_at, host, available, live, status, job_id, parent_node_id, parent_link_source, fork, fork_of, resume_command, tokens, cost_usd, summary, first_prompt, last_prompt, final_message, transcript_path, url, ... }, prompts, commits, files_edited, plan_docs, notes, parent, children (sessions it spawned) }. notes are the notes saved from that session and the notes linked to it with link_note, newest first, each { id, excerpt, tags, created_at, kind: "made" | "linked" }; a note that is both is listed once as "made". A fork (parent_link_source "fork") is a session Claude Code copied from its parent with --fork-session or as a background job: fork is { parent_node_id, forked_at, prompt_count } and fork_of says "fork of <parent node id> (after prompt N, <local time>)"; both are null for any other session. resume_command is the way back into the session from a terminal on this machine: "claude attach <job_id>" while it runs as a Claude Code background job (job_id set), else "claude --resume <session_id>"; null when it ran on the other machine. available: false means it ran on the other machine (host).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Session node id like A0-3G: two characters, a dash, two characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note id (A-B32). |

### `session_transcript`

**Search a session transcript** · read-only

Search one Claude Code session's own transcript for words and get the matching messages: { node_id, session_id, query, transcript_path, starts_at_fork_point, matches: [{ line, at, role, excerpt }], total_matches, truncated }. Every word must appear; "quoted phrases" stay together. Without query, the last messages come back. line is the line number in the transcript file. On a fork (session_get shows fork_of), only what the fork added is searched: the history it copied from its parent is skipped and starts_at_fork_point is true; search the parent node for that history. Works only on the machine that ran the session; elsewhere it answers not_on_this_machine (use session_get there).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Session node id like A0-3G: two characters, a dash, two characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note id (A-B32). |
| `query` | string |  | Words to find in the transcript. Omit for the last messages. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many matching messages (the most recent ones), 1-100. Default 20. |

### `sessions_usage`

**Claude Code token usage** · read-only

Token and cost totals of Claude Code sessions. by "month" (default): one row per month { month, sessions, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd }, newest first. by "node": the sessions that used the most tokens, with node_id, title and url. Optional repo and month (YYYY-MM, in the daemon timezone) filter both; totals covers every matching session.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` | "month" \| "node" |  | "month" (default) or "node". |
| `repo` | string |  | Only this repository, e.g. "mcp-notes". |
| `month` | string |  | Only sessions started in this month, YYYY-MM. |
| `limit` | integer |  | by "node": how many sessions, 1-200. Default 20. |

### `link_note`

**Link a note to a Claude Code session**

Link an existing note to a Claude Code session, so session_get and the wall's project graph list it with that session's notes as kind "linked" ("/n link A-B32 into A0-3G"). note_id is a note id like A-B32, node_id a session node id like A0-3G; both are case-insensitive and the dash may be omitted. The note itself (body, tags, origin) does not change. Linking again is a no-op. A deleted note cannot be linked: restore it first. Returns { note_id, node_id, session_id, linked: true, changed, made }: changed false means the link already existed; made true means the note was saved from that session, so it is listed there as "made" anyway.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `note_id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32: one character, a dash, three characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a session node id (A0-3G). |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Session node id like A0-3G: two characters, a dash, two characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note id (A-B32). |

### `unlink_note`

**Unlink a note from a Claude Code session**

Remove a link made with link_note between a note (note_id like A-B32) and a Claude Code session (node_id like A0-3G). The note itself does not change, and a note saved from that session stays listed there as "made" (origin is not a link). Unlinking what is not linked is a no-op. Returns { note_id, node_id, session_id, linked: false, changed, made }: changed false means there was no link.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `note_id` | string | yes | Note id like A-B32: one character, a dash, three characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a session node id (A0-3G). |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Session node id like A0-3G: two characters, a dash, two characters. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. Not a note id (A-B32). |

### `session_resume`

**Resume a Claude Code session**

Open a Claude Code session from the session graph in the user's tmux, on this machine. node_id is a session node id like A0-3G (two characters, a dash, two characters; not a note id). If that session is already running, its tmux window is focused and prompt (if given) is typed into it; it is never resumed twice. If it is running as a Claude Code background job (claude --bg, a forked job), its attach window is focused (prompt typed into it), or, when none is open, a new window runs `claude attach <job>` and the answer is action attached with job_id; a prompt given then is not delivered (prompt_delivered: false), so call again with it once the window is up. Otherwise a new window in the most recently attached tmux session runs `claude --resume <session> [prompt]` in the session's directory; if that directory is gone (a removed worktree) it runs from the repository checkout and returns original_cwd. fresh=true starts a new session instead of resuming: notesd writes a handoff file under its data dir (handoffs/) holding the node id, title, cwd and repo, transcript path, the stored summary with its age, plan docs, commits, the cwd's git status and git diff --stat, and every stored prompt with Claude's reply to it (when they do not fit half the node's context window, the first exchange and the newest ones that fit, with a note of how many were left out), loads it with --append-system-prompt-file, and sends a short first prompt that names the node and the file, then prompt as the task. A session whose transcript lives on the other machine answers not_on_this_machine. Returns { action: focused | messaged | resumed | spawned | attached, window, job_id? }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Session node id like A0-3G. Case-insensitive; the dash may be omitted. |
| `prompt` | string |  | Optional message: typed into the running session, or sent as the first turn after resuming. |
| `fresh` | boolean |  | true: start a new session carrying this node's handoff (summary, commits, git state, stored prompts and Claude's replies) instead of resuming it. Default false. |

### `expenses_spending`

**Spending in a date range** · read-only

Spending from expense-tracking (the user's own expense app; amounts in Indonesian rupiah) for an inclusive range of WIB (Asia/Jakarta) calendar days, in one call. Returns total_idr, item_count, group_count (expense groups = one pasted receipt/outing), average_per_day_idr, by_category (slug, Indonesian label, total_idr, share_pct), by_day (only days with spending, with weekday), by_week (every ISO week Monday-Sunday the range touches, keyed by its Monday, zero-filled; weeks cut by the range have partial=true and fewer days_in_range), and largest_items (biggest single items with group_title, occurred_on and group_id; pass group_id to expenses_get for the whole receipt). All money is integer rupiah, never converted. Pass categories to narrow the question, so "how much on meals in October and which week was worst" is one call (from 2026-10-01, to 2026-10-31, categories ["meals"], then compare by_week, minding partial weeks). "This week" is Monday through today (today_wib is in the result). Ranges up to 366 days; for month-by-month trends use expenses_months. Read the numbers for what they show (what dominated, unusual days, big one-offs) rather than only restating totals.

Slugs (Indonesian label): meals (Makan Harian), jajan (Jajan), dining (Fancy Makan Berat), snacks (Snack), drinks (Beverage), transport (Transport), fuel (Bensin), parking (Sewa Parkir Motor), bills (Tagihan), internet (Internet), utilities (Listrik & Air Apart), housing (Tempat Tinggal), entertainment (Hiburan), cinema (Bioskop), health (Kesehatan), grooming (Pangkas Rambut), other (Lainnya). "meals" is everyday meals only; for all eating and drinking pass meals, jajan, dining, snacks, drinks. |
| `top` | integer |  | How many largest items to return (default 10, max 50). |

One expense group from expense-tracking by id (a group is one pasted receipt or outing, e.g. "bakar duit tuesday"): title, WIB date (occurred_on), note, raw_text (the text the user originally pasted), its items in the app's order with integer-rupiah amount_idr and category (slug + Indonesian label), total_idr, item_count, and its photos (photo_count and public blob_url for each). Monthly spending totals from expense-tracking for the last N months ending at to_month (default: the current WIB month), oldest first, zero-filled so a month with no spending shows 0, the same series as the app's monthly chart. Months are WIB calendar months on the expense date; money is integer rupiah. Each month has total_idr, item_count, group_count and status: complete, in_progress (month to date, so not comparable to a full month as is) or future. average_per_month_idr averages complete months only. Optional categories filter. Use it for trends and this-month-vs-last-month; use expenses_spending for one period in detail (categories, days, weeks, largest items).

Slugs (Indonesian label): meals (Makan Harian), jajan (Jajan), dining (Fancy Makan Berat), snacks (Snack), drinks (Beverage), transport (Transport), fuel (Bensin), parking (Sewa Parkir Motor), bills (Tagihan), internet (Internet), utilities (Listrik & Air Apart), housing (Tempat Tinggal), entertainment (Hiburan), cinema (Bioskop), health (Kesehatan), grooming (Pangkas Rambut), other (Lainnya). "meals" is everyday meals only; for all eating and drinking pass meals, jajan, dining, snacks, drinks. |

One read-only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) against seer: the owner's quantitative trading lab: paper strategies, positions, trades, a leaderboard, and Sera, the method lab (lab.sqlite). ### `seer_leaderboard`

**Seer leaderboard** · read-only

Seer's paper-trading leaderboard, ranked the way the Seer app ranks it. Strategies are compared only over the dates every ranked strategy has an equity snapshot (the common window, returned as window.from / window.to / window.sessions); a ranking needs at least 63 shared sessions, and a strategy that overlaps too little is dropped so the rest can still be ranked. Order: annualised Sharpe of daily returns over the window (rf = 0, x sqrt(252)) highest first, no Sharpe last; then window total return; then smaller max drawdown; then id. ranked[] has rank, window figures (total_return, cagr, max_drawdown, sharpe) and since_start figures over the whole record (total_return, max_drawdown, win_rate, profit_factor where "infinite" means no losing trade, trades, months), plus sessions, days, paper_start and current_equity_usd. not_ranked[] holds the benchmark (SPY, the yardstick, with its figures over the same window), retired strategies (record kept, never ranked) and strategies too new to share 63 sessions, each with not_ranked_reason. Returns are fractions (0.12 = +12%); money is USD. Every return, drawdown and Sharpe excludes the owner's monthly top-ups (deposits are not performance), as the Seer app does; current_equity_usd is the real balance, top-ups included. Always name the window when you say which strategy leads. If window is null nothing is ranked yet: say so, and use shared_sessions to say how far off a ranking is.

No arguments.

### `seer_positions`

**Seer open positions** · read-only

Open paper positions in Seer, grouped by strategy (live strategies are listed even when flat). bracket[] holds open bracket orders: entry, mark (the order's own mark, else the symbol's latest stored close, else the fill price; mark_source says which), take_profit / stop_loss, day N of max_days, value, weight of equity, unrealised P&L = (mark - entry) x shares. book[] holds book and benchmark holdings: value, cost, income (dividends), unrealised P&L = value + income - cost (fees included), exit_pending when a sell executes at the next open. Each strategy also has equity_usd, open_value_usd and unrealised_pnl_usd. Money is USD exactly as Seer stores it; fx.usd_idr is the latest stored rate if the user wants rupiah. Pass strategy (an id such as 'RAW35-FR-GT'; seer_leaderboard lists them) for one strategy. include_pending adds what is queued for the next session: pending bracket orders, or a book strategy's target weights for its pending decision session.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | string |  | A strategy id, e.g. 'RAW35-FR-GT' (case-insensitive). Omit for every live strategy. |
| `include_pending` | boolean |  | Also list orders and book targets queued for the next session. Default false. |

### `seer_sera_best`

**Sera best variant per method** · read-only

The best Sera research result per method, read from Seer's lab (lab.sqlite). Each method's best variant is chosen by the lab's own rule: the dev-window trial with the highest MAR (CAGR / max drawdown), ties to the earlier trial; never chosen on DSR. Methods are listed best MAR first. Per method: name, family, status, hypothesis (shortened), dev_trials (how many dev variants it ran), and best: the trial's candidate_id, run_at, window dates, total_return, cagr, max_drawdown, profit_factor, trades, sharpe, mar, dsr, n_trials_at_run, spy_tr_return (SPY total return over the same window), funding (money-weighted returns when the trial was funded with deposits) and hurdles recomputed from those numbers (beats SPY, money-weighted when funded; PF >= 1.3; trades >= 100). test_trials[] lists the out-of-sample test-window trials for that method, if any. eligible_at_run is the lab verdict AS OF THE RUN DATE: the deflated Sharpe discounts for how many trials had been run, so a variant eligible then may not clear the bar at today's larger trial count, and this tool does not re-derive DSR. Say "eligible when it ran" rather than "eligible". Filters: status (method status), only_eligible (choose each method's best among trials stored eligible), limit (default 25). Returns are fractions.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many methods to return, best MAR first. Default 25. |
| `status` | "idea" \| "registered" \| "rejected" \| "dev-eligible" \| "promoted" \| "test-passed" \| "test-failed" \| "paper" \| "blocked-data" |  | Only methods in this lab status, e.g. "dev-eligible". |
| `only_eligible` | boolean |  | Pick each method's best among trials the lab stored as eligible when they ran. Default false. |

### `dword_vocab_lookup`

**Look up a dword vocab entry** · read-only

Checks whether the user already holds a word or phrase in daily-words (dword), their personal vocabulary app, before adding it. Matches in order: the exact term; the original (often non-English) word that resolved to an English term (origin_term); an inflected form of the same single word (studying/study); a near-identical spelling (naïve/naive), returned as candidates rather than a confident match since the user may still want to add it separately. Call this before dword_vocab_add.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `term` | string | yes | The word or phrase to look up, exactly as the user typed it. |

### `dword_vocab_add`

**Add a dword vocab entry**

Adds a complete vocab entry to daily-words (dword): part_of_speech, pronunciation, definition and exactly 3 example sentences are written as given — this tool makes no model call, so write a correct, complete entry yourself before calling it. On a term the user already holds, nothing new is inserted and the existing entry is returned instead (created: false). Pass origin only for a non-English term you already resolved to English (origin.term is the original word, origin.language its language, origin.context an optional "as in ..." sentence). Pass context (not origin) for a plain English term with a "> sentence" from /v — it is stored as the entry's own origin (origin_language "English") so the sentence is not lost; if the term already exists with no origin, the context is attached to it instead of failing. Refuses past 50 adds in a rolling 24 hours.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `term` | string | yes | The word or phrase to add, exactly as the user typed it. |
| `part_of_speech` | "noun" \| "verb" \| "adjective" \| "adverb" \| "pronoun" \| "preposition" \| "conjunction" \| "interjection" \| "determiner" \| "phrase" \| "idiom" \| "phrasal verb" \| "abbreviation" \| "other" | yes | The term's part of speech. |
| `pronunciation` | string | yes | A short pronunciation guide (IPA or respelling), e.g. "JEN-teel". |
| `definition` | string | yes | A plain-English definition, one sentence. |
| `examples` | string[] | yes | Exactly 3 example sentences using the term. |
| `origin` | object |  | Only for a non-English lookup you already resolved to term. Omit for a plain English add. |
| `origin.term` | string | yes | The original (often non-English) word or phrase, before resolving to term. |
| `origin.language` | string | yes | The origin language, e.g. "Indonesian". |
| `origin.context` | string |  | An "as in ..." sentence for the origin term (same length rule as context). |
| `context` | string |  | An "as in ..." sentence from /v's "> sentence" for a plain English term. Mutually exclusive with origin. |

### `dword_journal_find_similar`

**Find a similar daily-words journal entry** · read-only

Checks whether the owner's daily-words journal already has this saying or something close to it. Layer 1: an exact match after normalizing whitespace, smart quotes and accents (a re-paste of the same line). Layer 2, only on a Layer 1 miss: cosine distance of a fresh embedding against the owner's own entries, verdict 'duplicate' when distance < 0.25. A failed or unavailable embedding call never errors - it reports layer2_skipped: true and verdict 'none', since Layer 1 already ran and a provider outage must never block a save (dword's own rule). Returns { verdict: 'duplicate' | 'none', entries, layer2_skipped? }; entries holds the matching line(s) with their stored insight. Call this before dword_journal_add to decide what to tell the user; dword_journal_add runs the identical check itself, so this tool is for showing the user what would happen, not a required first call.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | The journal line (the saying), 2-1000 characters. |

### `dword_journal_add`

**Add a daily-words journal entry**

Adds a journal entry to daily-words, after running the same duplicate check as dword_journal_find_similar. If a duplicate is found and force is not true, nothing is inserted and the match is returned (D3 - 'show it, insert nothing unless the user says save anyway'). Otherwise inserts with insight_status='ready' and, when an embedding was computed during the check, a journal_entry_embeddings row too - a failed or unavailable embedding never blocks the entry insert; it is simply skipped and dword's own backfill picks it up later. insight is written by Claude (D2): meaning plus 2-3 concrete everyday situations, English, dictionary register, no advice, no praise. Returns { verdict, inserted, entries, entry?, embedded, layer2_skipped? }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | The journal line (the saying), 2-1000 characters. |
| `source_note` | string |  | Where it came from, e.g. a book title. At most 200 characters. Omit if unknown. |
| `insight` | object | yes | Claude's own explanation (D2: dword's GLM prompts are not called). |
| `insight.meaning` | string | yes | The saying's meaning, 20-220 characters, dictionary register, no advice, no praise. |
| `insight.whenItApplies` | string[] | yes | 2-3 concrete everyday situations it applies to, each 8-120 characters. |
| `force` | boolean |  | Insert even though a duplicate was found. Default false. |

## Seer Adversarial

Guide: [adversary.md](../adversary.md)

### `adversary_overview`

**Seer Adversarial overview** · read-only

Seer Adversarial: Claude reviews the picks of every method on Seer's roster before they are bought, and each method has a Claude twin, a paper book that runs the same method but drops what Claude objected to. Returns roster (every method, active first, then retired), methods (each active method with a twin: returns.original / .twin / .spy, money-weighted with deposits included, over the twin's record since it started; objections.objected / .reviewed / .fell_after (objected stocks that then did worse than the kept picks); coverage: decisions reviewed in time, absent (nobody reviewed before the open, or too late), paused (the owner turned automatic reviews off), pending (not open yet); checklist.original / .twin: Seer's five go-live rules with Seer's own wording in seer.label / seer.val; a twin's backtest is 'na' because Claude knows how the past turned out), cause (twins ahead of SPY, extra_profit_usd beyond the originals, drawdown_delta_pts), latest (the newest objections and can't-tell verdicts with reasons, sources and the host that made them), last_review and reviewer (this machine's reviewer, null when it is off). Fractions: 0.054 = +5.4%. Money: USD. Quote the numbers as given; never compute or invent your own.

No arguments.

### `adversary_verdicts`

**Claude's verdicts on Seer picks** · read-only

Claude's verdicts on Seer picks: agree, object, or unsure (Claude could not tell, so the pick is kept). Each has the stock (symbol), the decision session it was for, a plain-words reason, numbered sources (url, publisher, fetched_at), the model, prompt_version, lens and host, and late: true when it was decided after the session opened (kept for the record, but the twin ignored it). Without session it answers each method's latest decision, so "what did Claude object to today?" is verdict "object" with no other filter. sessions[] gives each decision's coverage (reviewed, absent, paused, pending).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | string |  | A Seer strategy id such as 'A-GT' or 'RAW35-FR-GT' (any case). A twin's id ('A-GT-CX') means its original. adversary_overview lists them. |
| `session` | string |  | The decision session, YYYY-MM-DD (the day the stock would be bought). Omit for each method's latest decision. |
| `verdict` | "agree" \| "object" \| "unsure" |  | Only this verdict: 'object' (Claude dropped it), 'agree', or 'unsure' (could not tell; kept). |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many verdicts. Default 50. |

### `adversary_scorecard`

**Claude's record on one Seer method** · read-only

Whether Claude's objections were right for one method. record.points: for each objection whose horizon has passed, the stock's return over the method's own horizon (5 sessions for the daily dip-buy method, until the next rebalance for a book) against the average of the picks Claude kept on the same decision; gap_pts below 0 means the dropped stock did worse, i.e. Claude was right; outcome worse / same (within half a point) / better. record.summary counts them; record.pending lists objections still inside their horizon. duel (daily methods with C, Seer's news model): on the nights C and Claude disagreed, who was right, judged against the names neither blocked. Few calls cannot tell skill from luck; say so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | string | yes | A Seer strategy id such as 'A-GT' or 'RAW35-FR-GT' (any case). A twin's id ('A-GT-CX') means its original. adversary_overview lists them. |

### `adversary_redo_context`

**Redo a Seer Adversarial review: context and clock** · read-only

For /redo only. Says whether redoing Claude's review of one pick is still fresh: a verdict counts only when decided before the US open (09:30 New York) of the pick's session, so after that a redo is stale and nothing is written. Returns can_redo, a plain message, the clock (open_utc, open_wib, start_by_wib, minutes_to_open; state fresh | closing | closed), the existing verdict, and, when fresh, the facts of the pick, the method's lens and the rules to follow. When can_redo is false, stop and tell the owner the message in a sentence or two; do not research. strategy takes 'A-GT' or a short form like 'A'.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | string | yes | A Seer strategy id such as 'A-GT' or 'RAW35-FR-GT' (any case). A twin's id ('A-GT-CX') means its original. adversary_overview lists them. |
| `symbol` | string | yes | The stock's ticker, e.g. 'SLB'. |
| `session` | string |  | The decision session, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the next one that has not opened. |

### `adversary_redo_submit`

**Redo a Seer Adversarial review: write the verdict**

For /redo only. Writes your verdict on one pick to Seer, replacing the earlier one. Call it only after adversary_redo_context said can_redo and you researched with web search, opening every page you cite. The clock is checked again here and nothing is written once the session has opened. agree or object without at least one source becomes unsure. reason: at most 600 characters, plain words for a non-trader.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy` | string | yes | A Seer strategy id such as 'A-GT' or 'RAW35-FR-GT' (any case). A twin's id ('A-GT-CX') means its original. adversary_overview lists them. |
| `symbol` | string | yes | The stock's ticker, e.g. 'SLB'. |
| `session` | string |  | The decision session, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the next one that has not opened. |
| `verdict` | "agree" \| "object" \| "unsure" | yes |  |
| `reason` | string | yes |  |
| `sources` | object[] | yes |  |
| `model` | string |  | Your exact model id. |

## Movies

Guide: [movies.md](../movies.md)

### `movies_list`

**List movie and TV titles** · read-only

The owner's movie and TV library (files on both laptops, titles shared). Finds titles by words in the title or synopsis (q), production company (company, e.g. "Blumhouse"), a person in the cast or crew (person, e.g. "Margaret Qualley"), kind (movie | tv), state, and the day the owner finished it (finished_from / finished_to; giving either keeps only finished titles). "Blumhouse films I have seen this year" is company "Blumhouse" with finished_from = 1 January and finished_to = today. Returns { count, titles: [{ movie_id, id, kind, title, year, release_date, state, finished_at, last_played_at, rating, watched_at, companies, available, poster_url, url, ... }] }. movie_id (M-23T4: M, a dash, four of 0-9 A-Z) is the id the owner reads and types, so quote it when you name a title, as a markdown link to its url; id (movie-<tmdb id> or tv-<tmdb id>) is the internal key; url (<wall>/movies/<movie id>) opens the title on the owner's wall, and an episode's url opens its series scrolled to that episode. state: finished (the watched flag, moved into a Done folder, or played to 90%), in_progress, unwatched, dropped (file deleted partway), removed_unwatched (file deleted, never played), seen (opened in VLC, position unknown). Dates are ISO 8601 UTC. available: false means no file of it is on this machine. Then call movies_get for episodes, files and plays.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | string |  | Words in the title or synopsis. |
| `company` | string |  | A production company by name, e.g. "Blumhouse" (part of the name is enough). |
| `person` | string |  | A person in the cast or crew by name, e.g. "Margaret Qualley". |
| `kind` | "movie" \| "tv" |  | "movie" or "tv" (a series). |
| `state` | "finished" \| "in_progress" \| "unwatched" \| "dropped" \| "removed_unwatched" \| "seen" |  | Only titles in this state (see the description). |
| `finished_from` | string |  | Finished on or after this day: YYYY-MM-DD (a whole day in the daemon's timezone) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `finished_to` | string |  | Finished on or before this day (the whole day is included): YYYY-MM-DD (a whole day in the daemon's timezone) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many titles, 1-200. Default 50. |

### `movies_get`

**Get one movie or series** · read-only

One title of the owner's library, by movie id (M-23T4), title id (movie-467905, tv-247718) or name ("mobland"; a name that fits several titles answers ambiguous with the candidates' ids). Every title has a movie id and so has every episode of a series, with or without a file (seasons[].episodes[].movie_id). Given an episode's movie id ("what is M-0T77 about", "we are missing M-0T77") the answer starts with asked: { movie_id, what, episode: { season, episode, name, air_date, overview, state, has_file, present_here, ... } }, with only that episode's files and plays and the series as a summary per season. A series with more than 60 episodes (One Piece) answers with a summary per season too (seasons[]: season, episodes, first_episode, last_episode, finished, files_here = the episode numbers with a file on this machine as ranges, so a gap is a missing file): call again with season for that season's episodes, or with episode for one episode number ("One Piece episode 744" is title "one piece", episode 744). Returns the title (title, year, release_date, overview, genres, companies, credits: directors, writers, producers, creators and cast with character names, rating 0-5, watched_at, review_note_id and the review, state, poster_url, url), seasons (a series: seasons[].episodes[] with season, episode, name, air_date, state, deleted and progress per episode), files (every file ever seen, deleted ones too: id, host, path, season, episode, duration_s, state, available, first_seen_at, deleted_at = when the owner deleted it, done_at = moved into a Done folder, watched_at, last_play) and plays (every play event, newest first: started_at, ended_at, position_s reached, duration_s, season, episode, episode_name, source "live" = VLC started by notesd or "vlc_recents" = read from VLC's recent list). last_play is the newest play: "which MobLand episode did I watch last and when" is last_play.season / episode / episode_name / started_at, and it survives the file's deletion. Positions and durations are seconds; dates are ISO 8601 UTC. available: false means that file is on the other laptop (host).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes | A movie id like M-23T4 (a title, or one episode of a series; from these tools, never invent one), a title id like movie-467905 or tv-247718, or the title in words, e.g. "mobland". |
| `season` | integer |  | A series only: just this season (0 = specials), with every episode of it. |
| `episode` | integer |  | A series only: just the episodes with this episode number ("One Piece episode 744"), in any season, or in season when both are given. |

### `movies_history`

**Movie watch history** · read-only

The owner's play events across the library, newest first: { count, plays: [{ started_at, ended_at, position_s, duration_s, ratio, source, host, title_id, title, kind, file_id, season, episode, episode_name, file_deleted, file_deleted_at, url }] }. from / to filter on started_at ("what did I watch last night" is from = yesterday). title narrows to one title (movie id, title id or name). movie_id on a play is the episode that was played, or the film. A play outlives its file: file_deleted_at says when the file was deleted. position_s null means VLC was opened but the position is unknown. Dates are ISO 8601 UTC; positions are seconds.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string |  | Plays that started on or after this: YYYY-MM-DD (a whole day in the daemon's timezone) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `to` | string |  | Plays that started on or before this (a whole day is included): YYYY-MM-DD (a whole day in the daemon's timezone) or an ISO 8601 datetime. |
| `title` | string |  | A movie id like M-23T4 (a title, or one episode of a series; from these tools, never invent one), a title id like movie-467905 or tv-247718, or the title in words, e.g. "mobland". |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many plays, 1-200. Default 30. |

### `movies_continue`

**Continue watching in VLC**

Plays something in VLC on the owner's screen, on the machine that runs this server: VLC opens and notesd records the play, so call it only when the owner asked to play, resume or continue something. With title (movie id, title id or name; "continue MobLand"): an episode's movie id ("play M-0T77") plays exactly that episode (resumed when it was left partway; missing when it has no file here); otherwise it resumes the latest unfinished episode or film from where it stopped; else starts the next episode whose file is on this machine; else plays nothing and answers which next episode is missing (missing) and which later episodes are present (present). Without title ("continue what I watched last night"): the same for the title of the newest play event. With random: true and no title ("play something", "I am eating dinner, play a random movie", "let's watch something"): the server picks one title at random among every film and series that can be played on this machine right now (a file here that is not deleted; not finished; a half-watched one resumes) and plays it, so do not list or choose titles yourself; picked_from says how many it chose among. Calling again picks again. Returns { action: resumed | started | missing | nothing | ambiguous | no_match, message, title, file, position (the second it starts at), missing, present, reason, candidates, movie_id (the episode or film it is about), url }. ambiguous lists candidates (call again with one id); no_match means nothing fits (or, without title, nothing was ever played). Errors: not_on_this_machine (the file is on the other laptop: play it there), player_unavailable (VLC cannot be started here), file_missing (the library lists the file but it is not on disk: a bug, tell the owner), not_found and ambiguous (no single title matches).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string |  | The title to continue, as an id or in words ("mobland"). Omit to continue whatever was played last. |
| `random` | boolean |  | true: play a title picked at random among everything playable on this machine ("play something"). Not with title. |

### `movies_person`

**A person's filmography, marked seen or not** · read-only

A person's filmography from TMDB with each entry marked against the owner's library, for recommendations ("recommend other Margaret Qualley films", "what else did this director make"). name finds the person (the most popular match); other_people lists others with a similar name, and person_id picks one of them. Returns { person: { id, name, known_for }, other_people, counts: { credits, in_library, seen }, credits: [{ kind, tmdb_id, title_id, title, release_date, roles ("cast as Sue", "Director", ...), in_library, state, seen, started, url, tmdb_url }] }, newest release first. seen: true when the owner finished the title or opened it (state finished or seen); started: true when they began it and did not finish (in_progress, dropped); in_library: false means it is not in the library at all, so seen is false and url is null. role "cast" or "crew" narrows the list; unseen_only drops what the owner has seen. Recommend from seen: false entries and use web search for reviews or anything newer than TMDB lists. Reads TMDB over the network: tmdb_unavailable means this server has no TMDB credentials, tmdb_error that TMDB could not be reached.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | The person's name, e.g. "Margaret Qualley". |
| `person_id` | integer |  | A TMDB person id from other_people, to pick that person instead of the most popular match. |
| `role` | "any" \| "cast" \| "crew" |  | "cast" (acted in), "crew" (directed, wrote, produced, ...) or "any" (default). |
| `unseen_only` | boolean |  | true: leave out the titles the owner has seen. |
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many credits, 1-200. Default 60. |

### `movies_mark`

**Mark a title watched, rate or review it**

Sets the owner's own marks. On a title (title = movie id, title id or name; an episode's movie id takes watched only and marks that episode): watched (true sets the watched flag, which makes the title finished even when the credits were skipped; false clears it), rating (0-5 stars as a whole number; null clears it) and review (plain text; saved as a note tagged #movie and linked to the title, so it is searchable like any note; it replaces the earlier review). On one file (file_id from movies_get files[].id, e.g. one episode): watched only. Pass exactly one of title or file_id, and at least one change. Returns { title_id, title, state, watched_at, rating, review_note_id, url } after the change, plus file for file_id.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string |  | A movie id like M-23T4 (a title, or one episode of a series; from these tools, never invent one), a title id like movie-467905 or tv-247718, or the title in words, e.g. "mobland". |
| `file_id` | integer |  | One file (an episode), from movies_get files[].id. Takes watched only. |
| `watched` | boolean |  | true: set the watched flag; false: clear it. |
| `rating` | integer \| null |  | Stars, 0-5, whole numbers. null clears the rating. |
| `review` | string |  | The owner's review as plain text. Replaces the earlier review; saved as a note tagged #movie. |
